claims.claim: Higgins quotes Young that Martin's narrative is shot through with references to and insinuations of a cleaner, nobler past.
claims.source: Joseph Rex Young, quoted at p.67 in Andrew Higgins's review, Journal of Tolkien Research 18.1 (2023)
claims.quote: references to and insinuations of a cleaner, nobler past

claims.claim: Higgins reports that Honegger applies Hemingway's literary iceberg to Martin, the idea that stories are strengthened by leaving things or events out.
claims.source: Andrew Higgins, review, Journal of Tolkien Research 18.1 (2023), reporting Thomas Honegger
claims.quote: stories are strengthened by leaving things or events out

claims.claim: Higgins reports Honegger's finding that Martin invented his world from the top down, with the backstories invented after the main narratives.
claims.source: Andrew Higgins, review, Journal of Tolkien Research 18.1 (2023), reporting Thomas Honegger
claims.quote: with the backstories being invented after the main narratives

claims.claim: Higgins reports Honegger's argument that Martin's in-narrative poems create the sense of an older transmitted oral tradition.
claims.source: Andrew Higgins, review, Journal of Tolkien Research 18.1 (2023), reporting Thomas Honegger
claims.quote: the sense of an older transmitted oral tradition

claims.claim: Higgins reproduces Martin's own statement, cited by Honegger, that he does not have a gift for languages.
claims.source: George R. R. Martin, interview quoted by Honegger at p.159, reproduced in Higgins's review, Journal of Tolkien Research 18.1 (2023)

claims.claim: Higgins reports Honegger's finding that Martin's language invention amounts to a handful of invented words for the Dothraki.
claims.source: Andrew Higgins, review, Journal of Tolkien Research 18.1 (2023), reporting Thomas Honegger
claims.quote: a handful of invented words for the Dothraki

claims.claim: Beveridge and Shan built their A Storm of Swords character network on 107 vertices representing characters.
claims.source: Andrew Beveridge and Jie Shan, 'Network of Thrones', Math Horizons 23.4 (2016)

claims.claim: Beveridge and Shan generated edges by incrementing a weight whenever two characters' names or nicknames appeared within 15 words of one another in the ebook.
claims.source: Andrew Beveridge and Jie Shan, 'Network of Thrones', Math Horizons 23.4 (2016)
claims.quote: appeared within 15 words of one another

claims.claim: Beveridge and Shan report that the King's Landing community accounts for 37 percent of their A Storm of Swords network.
claims.source: Andrew Beveridge and Jie Shan, 'Network of Thrones', Math Horizons 23.4 (2016)
claims.quote: community accounts for 37 percent of the network

claims.claim: Beveridge and Shan report that the network layout and colours identify seven communities in A Storm of Swords.
claims.source: Andrew Beveridge and Jie Shan, 'Network of Thrones', Math Horizons 23.4 (2016)

claims.claim: Beveridge and Shan report that betweenness centrality is the only one of their measures in which Tyrion does not come out on top.
claims.source: Andrew Beveridge and Jie Shan, 'Network of Thrones', Math Horizons 23.4 (2016)
claims.quote: the only measure in which Tyrion does not come out on top

claims.claim: Gessey-Jones and colleagues counted characters across the five books of whom 1,806 interact with another at least once.
claims.quote: of which 1,806 interact with another at least once
claims.page: Results, 'Evolution of the Social Network Structure'

claims.feature: other: cast size per unit of text

claims.quote: the number of characters per chapter settles at around 35
claims.page: Results, 'Evolution of the Social Network Structure'

claims.claim: Gessey-Jones and colleagues state that A Song of Ice and Fire is presented from the personal perspectives of 24 point of view characters.
claims.quote: presented from the personal perspectives of 24 point of view

claims.claim: Gessey-Jones and colleagues measured the 14 major point of view characters as having an average degree of 154.0 within the network of all characters.
claims.quote: have an average degree of 154.0 within the network
claims.page: Results, 'Evolution of the Social Network Structure'
